name: Combine several exams into one overall figure for each student
priorityReason: A report card and a transcript both need a figure across terms, and neither can be produced from one exam.

goal.capability: to weight the terms and combine their approved results into one figure per student
goal.outcome: the school has an overall standing for each student that reflects the whole year, not the last paper

Sees the cumulative result only for the subject or subjects they teach.

additional.description: A makeup is marked and an incomplete result resolves, which makes the cumulative figure recalculable.

A student with an outstanding excused absence shows as incomplete until the makeup is marked, rather than being given a figure calculated over fewer exams.
No position was calculated. Ranking is produced only by the merit list, and nowhere else.
A class incharge sees every subject for every student in their class; a subject teacher sees only their own subject.
The cumulative record is available to be carried onto the report card or transcript.
Nothing about the underlying exam results changed. The aggregation reads them and writes only its own figure.

businessRules.rule: Only approved results are combined. An exam whose results the Coordinator has not released is not part of anybody's overall standing.

Each exam or term carries a weight, and the weights together must total a hundred. A final term worth more than a first is a deliberate decision, and weights that do not total a hundred produce a figure nobody can interpret.
The cumulative total and percentage are calculated in a single action across every student in scope. Nothing is typed.
An exam a student was absent from carries its own absence rule into the cumulative figure. An unexcused absence contributes its zero; an excused one is left out of the exams counted.
A student with an outstanding excused absence shows as incomplete until the makeup is marked. A weighted figure calculated over fewer exams is not comparable with a full one.

What a teacher sees follows their role. A class incharge sees every subject for every student in their class; a teacher who teaches one subject and is not the class incharge sees only their own subject's result.
No position is calculated here. Ranking is produced only by the merit list, and a cumulative figure that quietly implied an order would compete with it.
The weighting used is recorded with the figure. A cumulative result produced under one weighting must stay explainable after the weighting changes.
The aggregation reads the exam results and never changes them. Correcting a cumulative figure means correcting a mark and running the aggregation again.
Re-running the aggregation replaces the previous figure and records that it was re-run, so a changed standing is visible rather than silent.
The cumulative record is carried onto the final report card or transcript, which is produced elsewhere.

alternateFlows.condition: A student has an outstanding excused absence
alternateFlows.behaviour: They show as incomplete until the makeup is marked. A weighted figure over fewer exams is not comparable with a full one (BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: A student's absence was classified unexcused
alternateFlows.behaviour: The zero contributes to the weighted figure and the result is complete, since nothing further is coming (BR-4).

alternateFlows.condition: A subject teacher who is not the class incharge opens the view
alternateFlows.behaviour: They see only their own subject's cumulative result, across the students they teach (BR-6).

alternateFlows.condition: A mark is corrected after the aggregation was run
alternateFlows.behaviour: The aggregation is run again. The previous figure is replaced and the re-run is recorded, so a changed standing is visible (BR-9, BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: A makeup is marked and the absence resolves
alternateFlows.behaviour: The student's incomplete figure becomes complete once the aggregation is run again.

alternateFlows.condition: The aggregation covers the whole session year
alternateFlows.behaviour: Every student in the session is combined in one run, which is what a transcript reads.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
